cells.tense: You are here with the work, giving it the time it actually needs.
cells.ask: Show one unfinished piece to somebody today, in the state it's honestly in.
cells.core:
You're tending something by practicing it — turning it over, checking it, letting it get more solid instead of just bigger. That's work happening now, not a down payment on some later payoff.

It's also why a change holds when one comes. The ground goes firm first, then the move. So the practice can have some play in it. Let one piece be seen before it's polished — not for a verdict, just so it isn't only yours. The next pass can wait an hour; being seen doesn't have to. Whatever comes back you can take or leave, and the piece is no worse for having been out of the room.
cells.sheetLine: You give the work its time, then the change holds.
cells.verb: Working it out slowly, testing it against the body until it holds

cells.tense: You are already living past the point where this gets finished.
cells.ask: Stop at one thing today and leave it unfinished on purpose.
cells.core:
You're refining past the point of use. Every round gets another pass, checked for the flaw that hasn't shown up yet, measured against a standard that keeps sliding forward — and the next pass is being treated as the one that finally settles it. It doesn't settle. The thing is already good and that fact has stopped reaching you.

A calmer shape of this has endings in it. Work gets finished, handed over, left alone, and the quiet afterward is what completion feels like from inside rather than a loss. You can see the finish line if you look. Set one piece down today while it's still imperfect and let that count.

cells.tense: You stopped bringing it out of the room some time back.
cells.ask: Tell one person the honest version of one thing you're working on, out loud, this week.
cells.core:
You still do the work. What's gone quiet is showing it anywhere. The method stays private, the careful attention runs with nobody watching, and none of it counts as care because none of it reaches anyone. At some point it stopped being worth the risk of being seen doing it.

Under all that is something simpler: give and take. You hand something over, someone hands something back, neither side keeps score. That's what feeds this — not more practice, not pushing yourself harder. Say one true thing to one person about what you're actually doing, even badly, even mid-thought. What they send back is the current that's missing.
cells.sheetLine: You're still working and nobody's getting any of it.

cells.tense: You are already setting how this gets made and calling it procedure.
cells.ask: Name one choice in your work today as yours — say 'I decided that' and mean it.
cells.core:
You decide how this gets done. What's worth keeping, what gets another look, what the standard even is — that's you in the moment, and it's been narrated as just the way the work goes. When it's going well this looks like a quiet confidence you carry without naming: you know why a thing is the way it is, because you settled it. That's the part that hasn't been claimed.

Nothing has to change in how you practice. What changes is that it stops being described as something that happens to you. The care you're giving this thing is yours to claim, and claiming it isn't bragging — it's just accurate. You can see how you'd want it to go, and that picture came from somewhere in you with a say in it.
